name: Schema Evolution & Database Migrations
description: Schema Evolution & Database Migrations standard. Defines enforceable rules, implementation boundaries, failure handling and review evidence expected when STD-DATA-MIG applies.

rules.title: Use expand–migrate–contract for breaking schema changes
rules.detail: Introduce backward-compatible schema first, deploy compatible code, migrate/backfill data, switch reads/writes, then remove old schema in a later safe release.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Use expand–migrate–contract for breaking schema changes.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Use expand–migrate–contract for breaking schema changes.

rules.title: Keep migrations deterministic and version controlled
rules.detail: Each migration is immutable after shared use, ordered, reviewable and applied by a controlled deployment process.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Keep migrations deterministic and version controlled.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Keep migrations deterministic and version controlled.

rules.title: Design migrations for production data volume and locking
rules.detail: Estimate runtime/lock impact, batch large backfills and avoid long blocking DDL on hot tables where the database provides safer alternatives.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Design migrations for production data volume and locking.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Design migrations for production data volume and locking.

rules.title: Define rollback or forward-fix strategy before release
rules.detail: For destructive or irreversible changes, document backup, compatibility window and forward remediation rather than assuming automatic down migration is safe.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Define rollback or forward-fix strategy before release.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Define rollback or forward-fix strategy before release.

rules.title: Separate schema change from business backfill when operationally safer
rules.detail: Long-running data transformations should run as resumable, observable jobs instead of blocking application startup/deployment.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Separate schema change from business backfill when operationally safer.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Separate schema change from business backfill when operationally safer.

rules.title: Verify migration state during deployment
rules.detail: Deployment must fail safely when expected migration prerequisites/version are missing and expose current schema version for diagnostics.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Verify migration state during deployment.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Verify migration state during deployment.

integration_guide.title: Resolve applicability and dependencies
integration_guide.description: Confirm where STD-DATA-MIG applies and resolve its extends/implements/uses/aligns_with dependencies in the project standard profile.

integration_guide.title: Record project decisions
integration_guide.description: Apply the rules of Schema Evolution & Database Migrations to requirements/design/ADRs and record any project-specific thresholds, providers or justified exceptions.

integration_guide.title: Implement with evidence
integration_guide.description: Implement the applicable MUST/SHOULD rules and link code, configuration, tests or review evidence to the change.

integration_guide.title: Verify before completion
integration_guide.description: Run automated checks where possible and manual review for judgement-based rules; close or approve documented deviations.

common_issues.issue: Deployment fails because old code sees the new schema
common_issues.cause: A breaking migration was applied in one step.
common_issues.solution: Use expand–migrate–contract and keep rolling-deployment compatibility.

common_issues.cause: DDL/backfill was not evaluated against table size and locks.
common_issues.solution: Use online-safe DDL, batching and a separately observable backfill job.
